# anatomy_Q89

## Question

Image shows muscle belly bulging on elbow flexion. Sign identified?

## Options

- A) Popeye sign ✅
- B) Hill-Sachs sign
- C) Rising sun sign
- D) Sulcus sign

## Your Answer

D) Sulcus sign

## Correct Answer

A) Popeye sign

## Key Fact (generated by LLM)

The Popeye sign is a clinical sign where the muscle belly of the biceps brachii bulges on elbow flexion, indicating a rupture of the distal biceps tendon. This occurs due to the loss of continuity between the biceps tendon and its insertion on the radial tuberosity, allowing the muscle to contract and bulge. The correct identification of this sign is crucial for diagnosing biceps tendon injuries.

## Why You Got It Wrong (generated by LLM)

The student incorrectly identified the sign as the Sulcus sign, which is actually a sign of shoulder instability.
